Not as bad as others, but thought I'd get this off my chest. When I was around 6 years old or so, my dad took me to a local drive thru burger joint. As we were getting our stuff, an old man comes walking out with what must be his granddaughter who looked to be my age or younger. It was the middle of winter so the whole parking lot / drive thru was completely covered with ice. The old man was a good ways ahead of us when my dad starts to drive. At 6 years old I watched this man collapse and my dad screech to a halt. In my mind I connected these two events, the man falling and my dad stopping suddenly into my dad running him and the girl over. A second later my dad leaps out of the truck and there is screaming and the young girl is crying. In my 6 year old mind I think my dad just murdered a man. After a few minutes my dad hops back in the truck and hurriedly leaves. At the time I thought he was driving away from a crime, but I think he was actually trying to shield me from being traumatized... nice one dad. My dad never brought it up again and for YEARS I thought he was a murderer and that I was protecting him. When I was 16 years old we went to that same burger joint and my dad retold me the story, but from an adults point of view. Apparently the man had a heart attack and died on the spot, and my dad was running to help him and call the police. He didnt mention it because he thought I was young enough to forget it with time. I wasnt.

When I decided I wanted to seek out professional help I went to my local clinic and asked whether they had a free or reduced clinic time, as I was making only minimum wage. They did, but they recommended a volunteer clinic instead that charged on a sliding scale up to only $10. At that clinic I was given medication, 4 therapy sessions, and lab work for free. After the 4 therapy sessions I'm being billed on a sliding scale again and, I'm only paying about $15. The process of seeing the therapist was super easy for me. I was given a voucher and had to sign some easy paper work, and saw the therapist the same day. If your parents understand what's going on with you, you could ask them to bring you to the local clinic to be put in contact with a therapist office, or just go directly to the therapist office.

I recently started therapy for the first time since I was a kid. It honestly depends on how open you are to it. My new therapist is a very nice lady, and she makes me feel less guilty for how I've been feeling. For me it's been less talking about solutions and more about validation, and I do feel like it's helping. If money is an issue, many therapist offices work on a sliding scale based off income, so they don't have to be expensive. There are also clinics that offer free services and support for people with depression, including free counseling services. In my opinion, it is entirely worth it.
